Cats: Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know about our feline friends

Why do cats purr?

Cats purr for several reasons: contentment when being petted, self-soothing when stressed or injured, and to communicate with their kittens. The sound is produced by rapid contractions of the laryngeal muscles at a frequency that may have therapeutic effects.

How many hours do cats sleep per day?

Cats are known for their love of sleep! They typically sleep between 12 to 16 hours per day, with some cats sleeping up to 20 hours. This is an evolutionary adaptation from their wild ancestors who conserved energy between hunts. Most of their sleep is light and can be interrupted quickly.

What is the best way to introduce a new cat to my home?

Introduce a new cat gradually. Start by keeping them in a single room with food, water, litter box, and toys. Let them adjust for several days before allowing exploration of other areas. Use vertical spaces (cat trees) for security. Introduce to other pets slowly and under supervision. Reward calm interactions with treats and praise.

How often should I groom my cat?

Grooming frequency depends on coat type. Long-haired cats should be brushed daily or several times a week to prevent matting and reduce shedding. Short-haired cats need brushing 1-2 times per week. Regular grooming also helps distribute natural oils, keeps skin healthy, and reduces hairballs. Most cats enjoy grooming once they're accustomed to it.

What should I feed my cat?

Cats are obligate carnivores and require high-quality protein. Both wet and dry commercial cat foods meeting AAFCO standards are appropriate. Choose age-appropriate formulas (kitten, adult, senior). Some cats have dietary sensitivities or health conditions requiring special foods. Always provide fresh water. Consult your veterinarian to determine the best diet for your specific cat.

How can I keep my indoor cat mentally stimulated?

Provide enrichment through interactive toys (feather wands, laser pointers), puzzle feeders, window perches for bird watching, and cat trees for climbing. Rotate toys regularly to maintain novelty. Consider clicker training or teaching tricks with treats. Play sessions of 10-15 minutes several times daily help keep cats engaged and prevent behavioral problems.

What are common signs of illness in cats?

Watch for changes in behavior including loss of appetite, increased thirst, lethargy, vomiting, diarrhea, difficulty urinating, excessive grooming, or changes in sleep patterns. Cats are masters at hiding illness, so subtle changes warrant veterinary attention. Other signs include weight loss, discharge from eyes or nose, and breathing difficulties. Annual check-ups help catch issues early.

How long do cats typically live?

Indoor cats typically live 12-18 years, with some reaching their 20s or beyond. Outdoor cats have shorter lifespans, averaging 2-5 years due to environmental hazards, disease, and accidents. Factors affecting longevity include genetics, diet, veterinary care, environment, and whether they're indoor or outdoor cats. Proper nutrition and regular veterinary care can help maximize a cat's lifespan.

Why do cats knead with their paws?

Kneading—pushing alternately with front paws—is a leftover behavior from kittenhood when they kneaded their mother to stimulate milk flow. Adult cats knead when they're happy and content, often while purring. It's a sign of affection and comfort. Some cats knead on soft surfaces, blankets, or their owners' laps. This behavior is completely normal and endearing.

What does cat body language tell us?

Learn to read your cat's body language. A straight, upright tail shows confidence and contentment. A low or tucked tail indicates fear. Flattened ears mean they're annoyed or scared. Slow blinks are a sign of affection—try slow blinking back! Dilated pupils can mean excitement or aggression depending on context. Arched back with puffed fur shows they're frightened or defensive.

+ Why do cats purr? +
+

+
+
+

+ How many hours do cats sleep per day? +
+

Cats are known for their love of sleep! They typically sleep between 12 to 16 hours per day, with some cats sleeping up to 20 hours. This is an evolutionary adaptation from their wild ancestors who conserved energy between hunts. Most of their sleep is light and can be interrupted quickly.

+
+
+
+ +
+
+ What is the best way to introduce a new cat to my home? +
+

+
+
+
+ +
+
+ How often should I groom my cat? +
+

Regular grooming also helps distribute natural oils, keeps skin healthy, and reduces hairballs. Most cats enjoy grooming once they're accustomed to it.

+
+
+
+ +
+
+ What should I feed my cat? +
+

Cats are obligate carnivores and require high-quality protein. Both wet and dry commercial cat foods meeting AAFCO standards are appropriate. Choose age-appropriate formulas (kitten, adult, senior). Some cats have dietary sensitivities or health conditions requiring special foods. Always provide fresh water. Consult your veterinarian to determine the best diet for your specific cat.

+
+
+
+ +
+
+ How can I keep my indoor cat mentally stimulated? +
+

Provide enrichment through interactive toys (feather wands, laser pointers), puzzle feeders, window perches for bird watching, and cat trees for climbing. Rotate toys regularly to maintain novelty. +
+
+
+ +
+
+ What are common signs of illness in cats? +
+

Watch for changes in behavior including loss of appetite, increased thirst, lethargy, vomiting, diarrhea, difficulty urinating, excessive grooming, or changes in sleep patterns. Annual check-ups help catch issues early.

+
+
+
+ +
+
+ How long do cats typically live? +
+

Indoor cats typically live 12-18 years, with some reaching their 20s or beyond. Outdoor cats have shorter lifespans, averaging 2-5 years due to environmental hazards, disease, and accidents. Factors affecting longevity include genetics, diet, veterinary care, environment, and whether they're indoor or outdoor cats. Proper nutrition and regular veterinary care can help maximize a cat's lifespan.

+

Cats: Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know about our feline friends

Why do cats purr?

Cats purr for several reasons: contentment when being petted, self-soothing when stressed or injured, and to communicate with their kittens. The sound is produced by rapid contractions of the laryngeal muscles at a frequency that may have therapeutic effects.

How many hours do cats sleep per day?

Cats are known for their love of sleep! They typically sleep between 12 to 16 hours per day, with some cats sleeping up to 20 hours. This is an evolutionary adaptation from their wild ancestors who conserved energy between hunts. Most of their sleep is light and can be interrupted quickly.

What is the best way to introduce a new cat to my home?

Introduce a new cat gradually. Start by keeping them in a single room with food, water, litter box, and toys. Let them adjust for several days before allowing exploration of other areas. Use vertical spaces (cat trees) for security. Introduce to other pets slowly and under supervision. Reward calm interactions with treats and praise.

How often should I groom my cat?

Grooming frequency depends on coat type. Long-haired cats should be brushed daily or several times a week to prevent matting and reduce shedding. Short-haired cats need brushing 1-2 times per week. Regular grooming also helps distribute natural oils, keeps skin healthy, and reduces hairballs. Most cats enjoy grooming once they're accustomed to it.

What should I feed my cat?

Cats are obligate carnivores and require high-quality protein. Both wet and dry commercial cat foods meeting AAFCO standards are appropriate. Choose age-appropriate formulas (kitten, adult, senior). Some cats have dietary sensitivities or health conditions requiring special foods. Always provide fresh water. Consult your veterinarian to determine the best diet for your specific cat.

How can I keep my indoor cat mentally stimulated?

Provide enrichment through interactive toys (feather wands, laser pointers), puzzle feeders, window perches for bird watching, and cat trees for climbing. Rotate toys regularly to maintain novelty. Consider clicker training or teaching tricks with treats. Play sessions of 10-15 minutes several times daily help keep cats engaged and prevent behavioral problems.

What are common signs of illness in cats?

Watch for changes in behavior including loss of appetite, increased thirst, lethargy, vomiting, diarrhea, difficulty urinating, excessive grooming, or changes in sleep patterns. Cats are masters at hiding illness, so subtle changes warrant veterinary attention. Other signs include weight loss, discharge from eyes or nose, and breathing difficulties. Annual check-ups help catch issues early.

How long do cats typically live?

Indoor cats typically live 12-18 years, with some reaching their 20s or beyond. Outdoor cats have shorter lifespans, averaging 2-5 years due to environmental hazards, disease, and accidents. Factors affecting longevity include genetics, diet, veterinary care, environment, and whether they're indoor or outdoor cats. Proper nutrition and regular veterinary care can help maximize a cat's lifespan.

Why do cats knead with their paws?

Kneading—pushing alternately with front paws—is a leftover behavior from kittenhood when they kneaded their mother to stimulate milk flow. Adult cats knead when they're happy and content, often while purring. It's a sign of affection and comfort. Some cats knead on soft surfaces, blankets, or their owners' laps. This behavior is completely normal and endearing.

What does cat body language tell us?

Learn to read your cat's body language. A straight, upright tail shows confidence and contentment. A low or tucked tail indicates fear. Flattened ears mean they're annoyed or scared. Slow blinks are a sign of affection—try slow blinking back! Dilated pupils can mean excitement or aggression depending on context. Arched back with puffed fur shows they're frightened or defensive.
